note: Kazakhstan: nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for 90, 30 or 14 days (several within a longer period: not modelled); the investment-country programme gives the EU, North America, Australasia, the Gulf and others 30 days (90 in 180). Everyone else may get an e-Visa (arriving at Astana or Almaty), except the 17 nationalities who must apply at an embassy. Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' own table of the visa regime by country and passport (updated 21 August 2026), column N (ordinary passports): it confirmed the rest and corrected Wikipedia's copy on Azerbaijan (90 days within 180), San Marino, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan (90 days, not 30), Barbados (28 days without a visa) and the Dominican Republic (60), both held before as e-Visa countries, and Mauritius (a visa on arrival). The table doesn't name Qatar, Libya, Palestine or Taiwan, and doesn't describe the e-Visa: those stand on Wikipedia's copy.

All European Union member states Australia Bahrain Canada Chile Colombia Iceland Indonesia Israel Japan Kuwait Liechtenstein Malaysia Mexico Monaco New Zealand Norway Oman Philippines Qatar San Marino Saudi Arabia Singapore South Korea Switzerland Thailand United Kingdom United States Vatican City ...
